minutes.headline: Parks Commission voted to draft three special town meeting articles: revolving fund change, rec director hours, Marshall Park funds.
minutes.summary: The commission heard recreation and Marshall Park updates and discussed capital planning and a Boys and Girls Club Polar Plunge. It learned the Finance Committee split on raising the rec director's hours and chose to seek town meeting instead. It voted to draft warrant articles, appointed a member to the Open Space committee, approved prior minutes, and adjourned.

public_comment.topic: Asked when the town can next apply for a Parkland grant; suggested a project other than Marshall Park.
Concern that closing the ball fields during phase one, and phase one omitting the parking improvements, will worsen parking; skate park access also.
Urged the commission to consider the Water District's properties near MCN, noting town right of first refusal.
Asked whether the Lake Shirley boat access issue was resolved; none known.

votes.motion: Draft warrant articles for the three items: change revolving fund type, additional rec director hours, remaining Marshall Park funds.
Appoint Tim to the Open Space committee as Parks Commission representative.
Approve minutes of the June meeting.

budget_items.what_was_said: Existing capital requests were read out; the lake treatment grant application to the state was not approved.

budget_items.what_was_said: Fees collected this year looked lower than prior years on the spreadsheet; Angela to check the registration counts.

budget_items.topic: Rec director hours increase from 19 to 28
budget_items.what_was_said: Select board approved; Finance Committee split and did not approve. Proposal was funding from the 53D revolving account.
Change would allow carrying balances and full-time salaries; interest would go to the town.
Quarterly grant for shovel-ready community projects, no match; could suit Marshall Park components.
The skate park group is still raising more money; project is privately funded.
Quotes received; may be paid by a donor or from the revolving account.
Commission to seek additional funding at fall town meeting, amount to be determined.

Chris to keep existing capital requests moving; a longer capital planning session set for a winter meeting.
Chair to ask the skate park group for an update for the next meeting.
Chair to draft letters to baseball and softball groups that Marshall Park fields will be unavailable in 2025.
Special meeting set for August 14; regular meeting tentatively August 21; signage on the Aug 14 agenda.
Boys and Girls Club to rejoin the commission in September about the Polar Plunge, tentatively Nov 30.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission voted by voice to draft warrant articles for a special town meeting on three items; the count was not audible.
The three articles cover a change in revolving fund type, additional recreation director hours, and remaining Marshall Park funding.
The commission said it prefers not to return to the Finance Committee on the director's hours, which the Finance Committee had split on, and will go to town meeting.
The commission heard that the Marshall Park fields will be unavailable in 2025, and the chair is to write to the baseball and softball groups.
A special meeting was set for August 14, with a regular meeting tentatively August 21; a vote to appoint a member to the Open Space committee was not audible.

why_it_matters: Residents may be asked at town meeting to vote on moving a recreation revolving fund to a type that carries balances forward and pays full-time salaries, and to fund more hours for the recreation director.
The Marshall Park articles ask for additional funding for a project that will close the ball fields in 2025, so the cost and the loss of field use fall on town meeting voters and local leagues.
watch_next: The special meeting on August 14, with signage on the agenda, and a regular meeting tentatively August 21.
The text of the three warrant articles, including the Marshall Park amount, which the minutes say is still to be determined.
